analysis: Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1602-2394). The visible file_changes show the only changed ranges are head 453-473, 3239-3242 and 3255-3286, i.e. cluster onboarding stop-count documentation. The units supplied here (head 1602-2394) fall outside those changed ranges, so they are unchanged surrounding context. I did not see the added text at 453-473 in full, and the 3239+ ranges were not supplied. The content examined describes GLM-5.3 admission and step-scratch pricing, capacity refusals, media limits, calibration and shape warmup, ChunkBatcher drop-without-sink behavior, SSD prefix cache publication ordering (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_TERMINAL_BEFORE_PUBLICATION) and paged KV segment retention. It contains no new endpoints, no plaintext leak paths, no change to the cache-scope or HMAC-keyed at-rest design (T-041), and no change to the 30-minute TTL. The claims about deferred step-scratch pre-reservation and early-terminal ordering are documentation only, with no code in this batch. The ChunkBatcher text notes that request-to-session identity is not enforced; this is a documented pre-existing property (T-008, TB-002) and not a regression introduced here. Open question for integration: the cluster stop-count control messages (ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked, darkbloom cluster stop) appear in the changed ranges but are not visible in these units. A reviewer should check them for authorization of remote stop requests between paired Macs, which touches a possible availability-control surface. This is a docs-only change, so no code security regression is established.
